themes.label: Heat
themes.question: Is it getting warmer or cooler?

themes.label: Water
themes.question: Is it getting wetter or drier?

themes.label: Sun and sky
themes.question: Is more or less sunlight reaching the ground?

variables.name: Air temperature
variables.definition: The average temperature of the air two metres above the ground, the height of a weather station thermometer.

variables.name: Hottest air temperature
variables.definition: The highest air temperature reached two metres above the ground during the period.

variables.name: Coldest air temperature
variables.definition: The lowest air temperature reached two metres above the ground during the period.

variables.name: Surface temperature
variables.definition: The temperature of the surface itself: soil, rooftops, ice or the top of the sea. Often called skin temperature.

variables.name: Rain and snowfall
variables.definition: The average amount of water falling as rain or snow each day, corrected against rain gauges.

variables.name: Surface soil wetness
variables.definition: How wet the top 5 cm of soil is, from 0 (completely dry) to 1 (completely soaked).

variables.name: Root zone soil wetness
variables.definition: How wet the top metre of soil is, where plant roots drink, from 0 (dry) to 1 (soaked).

variables.name: Evaporation from land
variables.definition: Water returning from the land to the air each day, by evaporating from soil and passing through plants.

variables.name: Snow depth
variables.definition: The depth of snow lying on the ground.

variables.name: Moisture in the air
variables.definition: Grams of water vapour in each kilogram of air near the ground. Also called specific humidity.

variables.name: Relative humidity
variables.definition: How full of water vapour the air is, as a percentage of the most it could hold at that temperature.

variables.name: Water vapour overhead
variables.definition: All the water vapour in the column of air above one square metre of ground, from the surface to space.

variables.name: Wind speed
variables.definition: The average speed of the wind ten metres above the ground.

variables.name: Surface pressure
variables.definition: The weight of the air pressing down on the surface.

variables.name: Haze and dust
variables.definition: How much tiny particles such as dust, smoke and pollution dim the view through the atmosphere. Higher means hazier. Called aerosol optical depth.

variables.name: Sunlight reaching the ground
variables.definition: The solar energy landing on each square metre of ground per day, with clouds and haze included.
variables.origin: GEWEX SRB to 2000, CERES SYN1deg from 2001

variables.name: Heat radiated down by the sky
variables.definition: Infrared energy sent down to the ground by the atmosphere and clouds. This is the greenhouse effect seen from below.
variables.origin: GEWEX SRB to 2000, CERES SYN1deg from 2001

variables.name: Cloud cover
variables.definition: The share of the sky covered by cloud, averaged over day and night.
variables.origin: GEWEX SRB to 2000, CERES SYN1deg from 2001
